- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) and forecast is above recent high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.25) and forecast is below recent low, increase forecast by 5–10% to counteract pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above 14-day moving average), apply a 3–5 day lag correction: reduce forecast by 2–5% per day until price stabilizes.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops 5%+ from recent peak within 5 days), adjust forecast downward by 2–4% for next 3–5 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is mixed (0.25–0.75) and forecast is erratic, use 14-day moving average as anchor for smoothing.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “negative” values, assume downward bias — add 1–3% downward adjustment to forecast.  
- If forecast consistently overshoots true outcome by > 3% for 3+ consecutive days, apply a “cap” rule: limit forecast to 10% below recent 14-day high.
